items.title: Rupee jumps 23 paise to 92.62 against US dollar during early trade
items.rss_summary: The rupee jumped 23 paise to 92.62 against the US dollar in early trade on Wednesday, buoyed by strong foreign-fund inflows amid a buying rush in domestic equity markets and sliding overseas crude oil prices. A strong American currency, however, capped gains in the local currency, forex traders said. In the interbank foreign exchange market, the rupee opened at 92.65 and climbed to 92.62 against the greenback, up 23 paise from its previous close. On Monday, the rupee declined from its seven-month high level to close with a loss of 23 paise at 92.85 against the US dollar. The Indian currency market was closed on Tuesday on account of Prakash Gurpurb Sri Guru Nanak Dev. The local unit logged a sharp gain of over 1.6 per cent in the preceding five back-to-back sessions since the closing level of 94.19 against the greenback recorded on November 13. items.title: IIFCL IPO: Govt to part sale stake, company to issue fresh shares
items.rss_summary: The government is looking to part sale its equity shareholding in IIFCL along with a fresh issue of shares by the company in the initial public offering (IPO), which is likely by the end of the current fiscal year, an official said. The Cabinet had earlier this year approved the IPO and listing of India Infrastructure Finance Company Ltd (IIFCL), and the work is on to file a draft paper with market regulator Sebi for approval. Without disclosing the quantum of stake dilution, the official said that while the government will reduce its stake by an offer for sale, IFCL will issue fresh shares to raise capital in the IPO. Set up in 2006, IIFCL is a wholly-owned government company providing long-term finances to viable infrastructure projects and is registered as a non-deposit taking non-banking finance company with the RBI.
